question.text: Brahmaputra PE Fund, a Category II AIF, is evaluating a Leveraged Buyout of a listed mid-cap packaging company held by Priya Industries. For the transaction to qualify as an LBO (as distinct from a growth-equity minority PE deal), what ownership/voting stake does the acquirer typically target?

answer.text: 26% or more (to trigger a mandatory open offer)
51% or more of share capital or voting rights
75% or more to pass special resolutions
Any stake above 10%, since LBO is defined by leverage, not stake size

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on Leveraged Buy-outs (p. 259), LBOs are buyouts financed with significant leverage in which investors typically seek a controlling interest of 51 percent or more of the share capital or voting rights of the target. The transaction combines control acquisition with significant debt that is usually secured against the target's assets. The Trap: 26 percent is the SEBI Takeover Code's open-offer trigger for listed companies, not the LBO control threshold. 75 percent is the super-majority special-resolution threshold under the Companies Act, again unrelated to the LBO definition. Stake size matters: an LBO is defined by both leverage and the 51 percent-or-more control stake, not by leverage alone. Note: The source explicitly anchors the LBO definition on p. 259 around control acquisition of 51 percent or more of share capital or voting rights, with significant debt secured against the target's assets.
